title: Love has boundaries
hookLine: love doesn't require letting yourself be harmed

lines: NO LEISURE SO MUCH AS TO EAT.
cards: People were coming and going, more of them than anyone could greet.
In the Gospel of Mark, the disciples have just come back and told Jesus all they had done and taught, and the place is so busy, the text says, that they had no leisure so much as to eat.

Nobody would blame a teacher for saying keep going, there's more to do. Instead Jesus says something else, and it's worth hearing on a day when the phone keeps buzzing and someone always needs one more thing.

teach.h: COME APART, AND REST A WHILE.
teach.b: First, the invitation. In the King James text Jesus tells them: "Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while." Apart.
Rest. In the middle of real need, with real people waiting. The Gospel doesn't treat this as a failure of love; it treats it as part of the work.
Luke's Gospel says, in a short line, "he withdrew himself into the wilderness, and prayed." The same teacher who healed and fed and taught also walked away from the crowd, on purpose.
Christians read this in more than one way, but the plain picture is a love with a shape: edges, and times of being unavailable. Third, the harder edge.

When Jesus sends his followers out, Matthew's Gospel has him tell them that where a house or a city won't receive them, they should leave, and shake off the dust of their feet. Not fight. Not stay and be ground down.
Leave, and keep the peace inside. Some readers find a principle in it: you can wish someone well and still walk out of their door. Fourth, what this means on an ordinary day.
Love doesn't require letting yourself be harmed. A boundary isn't a wall to punish someone.

teach.h: A LINE THAT TELLS THE TRUTH.
teach.b: It's a line that tells the truth about what you can carry. Saying no to one thing can be the way you keep saying yes to the people you love.
And if anyone listening is in a situation where love is being used to hurt them, a boundary may mean getting help from someone you trust.
That too can be love, including love for yourself.

how: Christians often point to the Gospel scenes where Jesus withdraws to pray as a pattern for rest and retreat, and people on many paths keep a sabbath, a quiet hour or a retreat as a protected time apart.

o: a dry wasteland where nothing could ever grow
where Jesus told his tired disciples to come apart and rest
a place of punishment where sinners were sent away

games.q: you're with the disciples. the crowds won't stop, and nobody has had time to eat. what does Jesus say?
o: come apart and rest a while.
games.why: "come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while." in the middle of real need, he gives rest.

practice: Let your shoulders drop and feel where your body ends, your skin, the chair under you, the floor under your feet; that edge isn't unkind, it's just where you are.
Bring to mind one place in your life where a healthy boundary is needed, and without planning a speech, let one clear, simple sentence form, and hold it gently, without anger.
If you pray, you can ask for courage in your own tradition's words.

wordCard.voice: Desert place. Where Jesus told his disciples to come apart and rest, even while the crowds still needed them. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: love has edges. Resting a while is part of the work, too. Until tomorrow.
